findings.evidence: `instance isFiniteMeasure_restrict_Ioc (x y : ℝ) : IsFiniteMeasure (volume.restrict (Ioc x y))` at upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Lebesgue/Basic.lean:213, inside `namespace Real` (lines 49–442); the file already uses `Real.volume_real_Ioc_of_le` from the same module (line 367), so it is imported.
findings.fix: Delete line 353; `exact memLp_const a` resolves the instance from `Real.isFiniteMeasure_restrict_Ioc 0 R`.
findings.issue: `have : IsFiniteMeasure (volume.restrict (Ioc 0 R)) := ⟨by simp⟩` re-proves an instance already in scope, so the reason `memLp_const a` applies is obscured by a local `simp`-derived instance.

summary: Proofs are mostly robust and readable, but the private `glue` definition is unfolded inline with `piecewise_eq_of_mem/notMem` at five separate sites (one of them an unfolding-heavy `simp [glued, glue, …]`), and `memLp_glue` hand-rolls an `IsFiniteMeasure` instance that Mathlib already provides.
